notes:
## Fixed

- Send to Amp now reaches the thread you sent it from. With Prologue open in two threads of the same project, comments sent from one could land in the other and then go back to unsent. Update the Prologue plugin when the review offers it

## Other

- `prologue --version` reports the real release version instead of 0.1.0

## New

- Prologue now runs inside Amp orbs as an Amp plugin. Click Prologue Review in a thread to open the orb’s changes in the Portal pane, comment on them, then press Send to Amp and the agent works through each comment and replies in the review. The README explains how to install it
- Reviews in Amp are shared: everyone in a multiplayer thread sees new comments, replies, and edits as they happen, each comment shows who wrote it, and the thread owner can edit or delete any comment
- If a Send to Amp never reaches the thread, its comments go back to unsent and Prologue shows the message to paste into the thread yourself
- Reviewing in Amp works on a phone: the toolbar shrinks to one row, and tapping a line number comments on that line or selects a range
- When an older copy of the plugin starts a review, a banner offers to update it: Update with Amp asks the agent to do it, or copy the prompt and paste it yourself
- Guide works with the Amp CLI when Claude Code isn’t installed, and its button says which one it uses
- `prologue show` flags comments whose code changed since they were written, and `--open` lists only the open ones

## Fixed

- A branch with uncommitted work but no commits of its own is no longer treated as merged and archived. Its changes stay reviewable, and an empty view offers Show uncommitted changes

## New

- ⇧-click Export to copy a prompt for an agent that can’t reach your Mac, like an Amp orb. The agent finishes with one terminal command that you paste locally to add its replies to the review
- `prologue import-replies` adds those replies. It checks every comment and commit first, adds nothing if anything is wrong, and skips replies a thread already has. Use `--dry-run` to preview

## Fixed

- Reviews of a detached HEAD (for example, an Amp live-sync checkout) now show your staged and unstaged changes instead of saying HEAD is merged
- The `prologue` CLI works in a detached checkout instead of asking for a review id

## New

- Export is now a single button: click to copy the review as JSON, or ⌘-click to copy it with the agent prompt
- Guide is now a single button: click to generate a guide, and click again to regenerate it. An orange dot still shows when the diff has changed since the guide was made
- Press Esc to cancel a guide while it's generating
- Press Esc to close the archived reviews panel

## Fixed

- Opening Keyboard Shortcuts or Archived Reviews from the menu now closes the other panel instead of stacking on top of it

## Other

- Markdown export has been removed from the app; the `prologue` CLI still supports it

## Fixed

- The window can now be dragged by its title bar, and double-clicking the title bar zooms it — like any other macOS window

## Fixed

- Lines revealed with the expand controls between hunks are now syntax highlighted, matching the rest of the diff

## Other

- A calmer, more focused look — the review and diff area now sit on a clean white stage, with the warm cream confined to the toolbar and sidebar
- Quieter diffs: hunk headers and expand-lines rows use neutral tones instead of blue and orange tints, so the code stands out
- Orange is reserved for the primary action, selection, and comment rails; Viewed checkmarks are now green

## New

- Orphaned comments stay with their file — when the commented lines leave the diff but the file is still present, the thread appears in that file's card with an Orphaned tag, its last known location, and the captured code; the bucket at the top of the review now only holds comments whose file left the diff entirely
- Text in rendered markdown previews can be selected and copied
- Comment on brand-new markdown files from the preview — click any paragraph to jump to its line in the source diff, ready to comment

## Fixed

- Links in markdown previews and release notes open in your system browser instead of navigating the app window away — cmd-click and middle-click included

## Other

- Security hardening across the app, CLI, and release pipeline: the window is pinned to the app origin, comment text can no longer inject terminal escape sequences into CLI output, database reads are read-only, and review data is validated at every boundary

## New

- What's New — release notes for every version, in the Prologue menu and shown once automatically after an update

## New

- Viewed files expand automatically when you click them in the sidebar or jump to them with ⌘P

## New

- Rich markdown diffs — markdown files can be reviewed as a rendered preview with change markers instead of raw text

## Fixed

- The Install 'prologue' Command Line Tool action works again in packaged builds

## New

- Check for Updates… in the Prologue menu

## New

- The welcome screen shows the app version

The first release of Prologue — a macOS app for reviewing git diffs before they leave your machine.

- Review any branch, base, or working-tree diff with virtualized rendering, syntax highlighting, and word-level change highlights
- Leave inline comments and threaded replies anchored to diff lines; threads re-anchor as the code moves and archive with the review
- Generated review guides that walk the diff in a narrative order
- `prologue` CLI (bundled, installable from the app menu) for reading reviews and replying from the terminal or an agent
- Keyboard-first navigation: j/k, n/p, ⌘P file jump, and a ? shortcut cheat sheet
- Auto-updates via GitHub Releases
